authoring.question: q-86587
authoring.value:
The complement of $R,$ denoted $\overset{―}{R},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $R.$ To represent $\overset{―}{R},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $R,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035973/assets/79900f22c35570b35cf10664768ecf4460a7953ddf7f91dac1893b3ce81339bf.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $a$ and $c.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $R.$ Therefore, the complement of $R$ is

$$
\overset{―}{R}={a,c}.
$$

The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overline B,$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $B.$ To represent $\overline B,$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $B,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035973/assets/daad235ef63e127e99bf3eec7b7bbe75fe6adb969f5b54ebb5a3fb010773b680.png)

$$
\overline{B} = \{ a,c,e,g \}.
$$
